passage: I'm Maria. Last Saturday I had a hundred rupees saved for a sticker album, but at the toy stall I saw a tiny plush elephant and thought of my little sister Simran, who hugs everything she owns. Nobody had asked me to buy anything. I counted my coins twice. There was exactly enough for the elephant. When I gave it to her she pressed it against her cheek, shouted "Mine!" and ran to show Mummy. I had thought I would miss the sticker album. Strangely I didn't. My chest felt warm for the rest of the day.

qa.q: What did Maria buy for Simran?
qa.a: She bought a tiny plush elephant.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling when Simran pressed the elephant against her cheek?
qa.a: A joy that was warmer than she expected, with no regret about the sticker album; her chest felt warm for the rest of the day.

qa.q: What could Maria remember about giving gifts to her sister?
qa.a: That the giving felt good because nobody pushed her, so she can say no when she does not want to give and give freely when she does 😊.

qa.q: How does Simran see the gift?
qa.a: She is delighted: she pressed it to her cheek, shouted "Mine!" and ran to show Mummy.

grounding: Illustrates a child freely spending her pocket money on a gift for her little sister and finding the giving joyful.
